name: Pinochle
tagline: Bid, pass cards with your partner, show your meld and take the counters.
rulesSummary: 48 cards: two each of A, 10, K, Q, J and 9 in every suit, ranked in that order (the 10 beats the king). Partners sit across; 12 cards each.
Bid in tens from 250. Once you pass you're out; if the other three pass, the dealer takes it at 250.
The winning bidder names trumps, takes four cards from their partner and passes four back.

Everyone's meld goes on the table. In trumps: run (A 10 K Q J) 150, royal marriage 40, each 9 (dix) 10. Other marriages 20; pinochle (Q♠ J♦) 40, double 300; aces around 100, kings 80, queens 60, jacks 40 (both of each: ×10).
If the bidders' meld plus all 250 points in play can't reach the bid, they're set at once. The declarer may also throw the hand in.
Play: follow suit and beat the winning card if you can; if you can't follow, trump — higher than any trump already played, if you can.

Aces, 10s and kings taken score 10 each, the last trick 10 more. Make your bid and score meld plus points; fail and lose the bid. The other side scores too, if it takes at least one point. First to 1500.
